title: RAW UNREVIEWED: delegated authority lets one actor's later act bind another participant
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED. Whole C0 documentary account: a principal authorizes an agent to undertake one bounded act toward a third party; the agent performs it and the resulting obligation belongs to the principal. Revocation before the act prevents that effect, while revocation after an already completed act leaves it intact. Actor, authority holder and obligation bearer remain separate participants. No legal source identification, target gloss or completed reading is claimed.

design.whole_account: P empowers A to make a bounded undertaking to T on P's behalf. A makes that undertaking. T's resulting claim is against P, although A uttered or performed the act. If P withdraws the authorization before A acts, that act does not bind P under this candidate's stipulated system; if P withdraws it after the completed undertaking, the existing claim remains. The account can end by discharging that claim, separately from withdrawing future authority.

owned_scope.target_nomination: Complete already owned f83r P1 record, 72 ZL groups, as delimited in GDT790 and retained by W91. No Q record or later paragraph is appended to manufacture a consequence.
owned_scope.exposure: Already exposed development evidence. Only primary scope summaries and receipt metadata used by this producer; no target-body file opened or new target query performed.
owned_scope.limits: Single-figure panel ownership does not identify a principal, agent or third party. Textual references must pay those roles. The existing loan proposal is a comparator, not an inherited dictionary.

multistep_consequence: Authorization establishes a bounded P-to-A relation without making P and A the same actor.
A's subsequent act toward T generates a T-to-P obligation only while that authorization applies.
Moving the same revocation before versus after the act changes whether the principal's completed obligation exists, even when participants and the physical act remain identical.
A later payment/discharge affects the obligation, while revocation affects future authority; the two updates are not synonyms.
design.observable_difference: A paid complete written account must name or refer to A as actor but P as the bearer of the later obligation, and distinguish prior revocation from later discharge. A direct-action model makes the actor bear its own obligation; a self-permission model lacks a third-party principal obligation; a custody-only transfer does not generate that obligation merely from an agent's act. This producer has not located those roles or consequences in the target.

novelty.difference_from_333: 333 is an issuer/grant/object/protection/attestation chain; its named procurator is a terminal documentary role. It does not define an independently acting agent whose authorized act creates a later claim against a distinct principal, with revocation-order sensitivity.
novelty.difference_from_335_361: Permission/debt belongs to the same institutional actor. This account requires three parties and a different actor/obligation bearer. The fixed six-action code and failed cross-leaf contract of979 are not reused or enlarged.
novelty.difference_from_372_424: Loan372 separates title, custody and return duty; sale424 separates contract, delivery and risk. Neither compact original design supplies authority delegated from one person to another whose act binds the principal. Related legal contents are not treated as duplicates merely by genre.
novelty.checks: Bounded searches for agency, delegated, revocation, procurator, principal/agent and authorization; compact show333/335/361/372/424; two duplicates queries; route-check delegated authority third-party revocation permission. Empty lexical results were supplemented by targeted charter/permission primaries.

assumptions: The account is a hypothetical normative system, not a claim about actual Roman, medieval or present law. Notice, ratification and retrospective cancellation exceptions are not silently imported.
P, A and T remain separate referents under one explicit global reference rule; no per-occurrence actor swap or invisible principal.
The relevant authorization, act, revocation and resulting obligation must all be written and paid in a whole account.
The completed-act versus future-authority distinction cannot be supplied only by an English rendering.
Directed reusable word composition, spaces, entry context and whole residuals remain obligations; no component or whole form receives a gloss from this producer.
why_it_could_fail: The passage may have no three-party structure or no expressed authorization, so a delegation interpretation is unsupported.
Repeated nominal roles might identify kinds rather than individual parties, leaving the obligation bearer unbound.
An unconstrained authority relation can merely relabel any process dependency; a later written principal-obligation consequence is required before selecting it.
Revocation-order contrast may remain observationally equivalent to generic action guards or no written comparison may exist. That is unresolved capacity, not refutation of all documentary readings.
design.smallest_next_step: If shortlisted, author one complete f83r P1 account with a fresh finite shared reference/construction proposal, retaining every unknown and alternative reading. Identify the exact written principal-agent-third-party relation and later obligation. Do not add a generic authority parser or acquire a new legal source merely to decorate the story.
design.decision_and_stop: A complete account with a paid distinct actor/obligation-bearer consequence can be shortlisted for fixed testing. If only authority labels or a direct action chain can be authored, park this offer; if generic guards yield the same world consequence, retain equivalence and select no meaning. RAW retention does not require previously confirmed names or authority glosses.
